title: The same advice for every generation: be mindful of Allah.
subtitle: One instruction given to all, and a Lord who needs no one

row.title: Allah needs my worship
sub: I am doing Him a favor

row.title: Free of need
sub: I am the one who gains

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah gave {idea}the same instruction{/idea} to the People of the Scripture before and to the believers: be mindful of Him and worship Him alone. If people refuse, everything in the heavens and earth is still His. He is {reward}free of need and worthy of all praise.{/reward}
now: You pray and somewhere inside a small voice says you have done Allah a favor today. {trap}As if He was waiting on you.{/trap} The verse turns it around. The whole universe is His. {idea}The prayer is for you{/idea}, like water is for the thirsty.
old: My worship is something I give to Allah.
new: My worship is something Allah gives to me, because He needs nothing.
try: Before your next prayer, thank Allah for letting you stand before Him.

title: He owns it all, and He is enough to trust with it.
subtitle: Allah as the One who manages your affairs
then: This is the second time in a short space that the verse says everything belongs to Allah. Ibn Kathir explains that He {idea}watches over every soul{/idea}, knows what it deserves, and witnesses all things. {reward}He is enough as the One who handles affairs.{/reward}
now: It is two in the morning and you are lying awake running numbers. The rent, the school fees, your father's medication. {trap}It feels like everything holds together only if you never stop.{/trap} Do your part, then put it down. {reward}Allah is enough to carry the rest.{/reward}
old: If I do not hold everything together, it will all collapse.
new: I do my part and leave the outcome with the One who owns it all.
try: Tonight before sleep, name your biggest worry and say: Allah is enough for me.

title: Nobody is irreplaceable to Allah. Your place is a gift.
subtitle: He can bring others in your place
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah can {trap}take people away and replace them{/trap} if they disobey Him. He links it to another verse: if you turn away, He will bring a people unlike you. Being part of His work is {idea}an honor, not an entitlement.{/idea}
now: You run the youth circle at the mosque. You started the charity drive. {trap}Some days you think it would all stop without you.{/trap} The verse is a gentle shake. {idea}Allah's work goes on with or without you.{/idea} Being used for it is the gift.
old: This good work would fall apart without me.
new: It is a gift that Allah lets me be part of His work at all.
try: Thank Allah today for one role you have in doing good, and do it humbly.

title: Want this world? Its reward and the next are both with Allah.
subtitle: Why settle for half the reward
then: Ibn Kathir addresses this to those whose ultimate desire is this life: {idea}Allah owns the reward of both worlds.{/idea} If you ask Him for both, He will enrich you. He points to the prayer for {reward}good in this world and good in the Hereafter.{/reward}
now: You are chasing the raise, the bigger flat, the new car. Nothing wrong with wanting them. {trap}But if that is all you ask for, you have asked too small.{/trap} The One who gives the raise also holds what lasts. {reward}Ask Him for both.{/reward}
old: I will focus on this life now and think about the next one later.
new: The same Lord holds both rewards, so I ask Him for both together.
try: Next time you make dua for something worldly, add a request for the Hereafter alongside it.

title: Stand for justice, even when it costs you or your family.
subtitle: Honest testimony that does not bend for anyone
then: Ibn Kathir explains that believers are to stand for justice and {idea}not fear anyone's blame{/idea} in doing so. Testimony should be exact, even if it harms you or your parents. Do not favor the rich or pity the poor, because Allah protects both. The verse warns against {trap}twisting your words or hiding the truth.{/trap}
now: Your brother scraped another car in the car park and asks you to say you saw nothing. Your manager wants you to keep quiet about a mistake that cost a colleague their job. {trap}Loyalty says bend.{/trap} The verse says {idea}the truth stands above everyone{/idea}, even the people you love.
old: Family comes first, even before the truth.
new: I serve my family best by not lying for them.
try: Notice one moment today where you are tempted to shade the truth for someone. Say it straight, kindly.

title: You believe already. Now believe again, and keep believing.
subtitle: Faith that is renewed, not just held
then: The verse calls people who already believe to believe. Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}not repetition but completion{/idea}: keeping faith alive and whole. He compares it to the believer asking in every prayer, {reward}guide us to the straight path{/reward}, which means keep us on it and increase us.
now: You said the shahada years ago, or were born into it. Since then it has sat in the background like an app you never open. {trap}Faith can go stale without anyone noticing.{/trap} The verse asks you to {idea}renew it, today, on purpose.{/idea}
old: I am already a believer, so this verse is not for me.
new: Belief is something I keep feeding, or it quietly fades.
try: In your next prayer, say guide us to the straight path slowly and mean it as a fresh request.

title: In and out, in and out, until the door stays shut.
subtitle: The danger of a faith that keeps switching
then: Ibn Kathir explains this as someone who enters faith, leaves, enters, leaves, then {trap}stays in disbelief and grows in it until death.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said it means they remain that way until they die. The verse describes {idea}where that pattern ends{/idea}, not a door closed on the living who turn back.
now: Ramadan you are in the front row. By Shawwal you have stopped praying. Next year the same again. {trap}Each time it gets a little easier to drift.{/trap} The verse is a warning about {idea}the direction of the pattern.{/idea} Break it while you still can.
old: I can drift for a while and always come back.
new: Every drift makes the next one easier, so I hold on now.
try: Pick one act of worship you dropped after a high season and restart its smallest version today.

title: The news for a two-faced heart is not good news.
subtitle: A warning about hypocrisy

row.title: tidings
sub: the word used for good news

then: Ibn Kathir links this to the verse before: hypocrites {trap}believe, then disbelieve{/trap}, and their hearts become sealed. They show loyalty to the believers in public and to the other side in private. The verse uses the word for good tidings, but {idea}the news is a warning.{/idea}
now: You are one person at the family dinner and a different one with your friends on Friday night. {trap}Each crowd hears what it wants.{/trap} The verse is not for pointing at others. It is a mirror: {idea}am I the same person in every room?{/idea}
old: Everyone acts a bit differently around different people.
new: There is a line between adjusting my tone and splitting my loyalty, and I watch it.
try: Think of one place where you hide your faith to fit in. Show one small sign of it there today.

title: Looking for honor in the wrong crowd? All honor is Allah's.
subtitle: Where real dignity comes from
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the hypocrites gave their loyalty in secret to those opposing the believers, {trap}hoping to gain honor and strength{/trap} from them. The verse asks: is that where you look for it? {reward}All honor belongs to Allah{/reward}, and He gives it to His faithful servants.
now: You laugh at a joke about your faith because the popular people at work are laughing. You drop your values to get into the right circle. {trap}It feels like moving up.{/trap} The verse says {reward}the honor you are chasing is not theirs to give.{/reward}
old: Being accepted by the important people will give me worth.
new: My worth comes from Allah, and no crowd can give or take it.
try: Notice one moment today where you trade your values for approval. Hold your ground gently.

title: When they mock Allah's words, do not stay seated.
subtitle: Staying silent in the room is a choice too
then: The verse refers back to an earlier instruction revealed in Makkah. Ibn Kathir explains that whoever {trap}stays and approves while Allah's verses are mocked{/trap} shares in what is being done. The instruction is simple: {idea}leave until they change the subject.{/idea}
now: The group chat starts making fun of the Quran. Everyone sends laughing faces. {trap}You do not join in, but you do not leave either.{/trap} The verse says the quiet seat is not neutral. {idea}Step out, or change the subject.{/idea}
old: As long as I am not the one mocking, I am fine.
new: Staying comfortable while my faith is mocked is a choice I am making.
try: Next time a conversation mocks what you hold sacred, change the subject or quietly step away.
